fixes.explanation: Judgment is the word. God presides in the divine assembly, and among the gods He renders judgment (Psalm 82:1). This is a courtroom scene, and God is the one presiding. The next verses show what He has to say.

No gift bags in this one, friend. The verse says God presides in the divine assembly and renders judgment among the gods (Psalm 82:1). That's a courtroom word, not a party word. The next verses show what He says to them.

Close, friend, but that's not the complaint. God asks, "How long will you judge unjustly and show partiality to the wicked?" (Psalm 82:2). The trouble is that they judge unjustly and favor the wicked. It's about how they judge.
Right on. God says, "Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless…" (Psalm 82:3). He tells the assembly to stand up for them. The very next verse keeps going with the weak and needy.

Not this time, friend. God says, "Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless…" (Psalm 82:3). The king and his officials aren't named in this verse. God points the assembly toward the weak and the fatherless.
Not this time. The verse says, "Defend the cause of the weak and fatherless…" (Psalm 82:3). Priests and Levites don't show up in this psalm at all. God's focus is on the weak and the fatherless.

Nothing in the psalm says that, friend. The reason is "…for all the nations are Your inheritance." (Psalm 82:8). Verse 7 does say, "like rulers you will fall," but the closing prayer gives a different reason.
